transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 1322 Tumbling Rapids Drive?
Yeah, this is me at 1322 Tumbling Rapids Drive, just me here, no one else, and the water’s not in yet—though I do have a boat if you need to get me out, no truck though.
Thanks for confirming your address and safety status. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
Just me here, all by myself, no one else around—so I’m good to go, no problem.

Thanks for letting us know you're alone and ready. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own, and I’m all by myself—no wheelchair, no oxygen, nothing like that, just me and the house, dry as a bone inside.
Is there water inside the home right now?
No, there’s no water inside the house right now—just me, and I’m good to go, no need to worry about flooding in here.
Thanks for checking in, staying safe is key. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
I’ve got a boat handy if anyone needs a ride out, but no truck or extra seats in a vehicle—just me and my own two feet here at 1322 Tumbling Rapids Drive.
Thanks for sharing your situation and offering help. Let me read that back: people at the home not confirmed; no water inside yet; you can help with a boat. Is that right?
Yeah, that’s right—just me here, no water in yet, and I can help with a boat, no problem.

Thanks for confirming and offering help with a boat. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
